name: capsule-fs
description: Filesystem tools for agents. Read, write, replace, grep, list, create, delete, move via VFS airlock. Part of Unicity AOS.
readmeExcerpt:
# astrid-capsule-fs




**Filesystem tools for [Astrid OS](https://github.com/unicity-astrid/astrid) agents.**

In the OS model, this capsule is the coreutils package. It gives agents the ability to read, write, search, and navigate the workspace filesystem through the kernel's VFS airlock.

## Tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `read_file` | Read file contents with optional line range (`start_line`, `end_line`) |
| `write_file` | Write content to a file |
| `replace_in_file` | Replace an exact string match in a file (rejects 0 or >1 occurrences) |
| `list_directory` | List entries in a directory |
| `grep_search` | Recursive content search with depth, file count, and match count caps |
| `create_directory` | Create a directory |
| `delete_file` | Delete a file (session-created files only, no whiteout support yet) |
| `move_file` | Move a file with 10MB size limit, existence checks, and rollback on failure |

All operations go through the VFS airlock. The kernel enforces path boundaries, copy-on-write isolation, and capability checks before any host filesystem access occurs.

## Development

```bash
cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release
```

aiSummary.oneLiner: Core filesystem tools and utilities for Astrid OS agents operating through the VFS airlock.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This capsule acts as the coreutils package for Astrid OS agents, equipping them with essential tools to interact with the workspace filesystem. It securely bridges the agent's operational logic with the kernel's Virtual File System (VFS) airlock, ensuring safe and restricted data access. The capsule provides specialized functions for reading, writing, searching, and manipulating files and directories. By standardizing these filesystem operations, it allows agents to reliably navigate projects, modify code, and analyze directory structures without compromising the underlying host system's security.
keyFeatures: Secure VFS access: Interacts with the filesystem exclusively through the kernel's secured Virtual File System airlock.
Comprehensive file operations: Provides discrete tools for reading, writing, replacing strings, and deleting files safely.
Advanced search capabilities: Includes a recursive grep-like search tool with depth, file count, and match count limits.
Directory management: Allows agents to list contents and create new directories within their permitted workspace.
Targeted replacements: Supports exact string replacement operations that strictly reject ambiguous matches.

useCases.title: Analyzing workspaces
useCases.description: Agents use the directory listing and grep search tools to map out a new codebase and find specific function definitions.

useCases.title: Automated refactoring
useCases.description: Code-writing agents utilize the exact string replacement and write file tools to apply targeted bug fixes safely.

useCases.title: Reading configurations
useCases.description: The agent reads specific line ranges from a large configuration file to understand project dependencies without loading the entire file into memory.

useCases.title: Managing temporary files
useCases.description: Agents create new directories to store intermediate data processing results and delete them upon task completion.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers creating capable, autonomous agents on Astrid OS that require secure, programmatic access to workspace files and directories.
